Issued at 400 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Currently Through Tonight...

Been a warmer, gusty start to the work week across the entire  
forecast area...and while the majority are sitting with
little/no cloud cover, satellite imagery showing a fairly 
thick batch of wildfire smoke passing through, keeping skies 
hazy. This smoke has remain in the upper levels, with no area 
automated sites showing any reductions in visibility, a trend 
that should continue the rest of the day. Looking aloft, data 
showing high pressure centered over AZ/NM...with a dampened 
ridge axis extending northeastward through the Central Plains 
toward the Great Lakes. Troughing/low pressure along the East 
Coast is keeping this ridging from sliding east...while low 
pressure over north-central Canada and southward extending 
troughing into the NNWrn CONUS is what has diminished the ridge 
strength. Satellite imagery showing a shortwave disturbance 
making its way east across the Nrn Rockies...which will aid in 
storm development with time this afternoon. At the surface, the 
gusty south-southeasterly winds are being driven by a tightened 
pressure gradient in place...set up between high pressure over 
much of the Midwest and an approaching cold front. This front 
currently sits from the southern NE panhandle up into central 
SD...with winds across the forecast area gusting around 25-30 
MPH. Temps are a touch warmer...with 3PM obs sitting in the mid 
80s to mid 90s.

At least scattered activity is expected to continue developing
along that surface frontal boundary the rest of this 
afternoon...with the main question going into this 
evening/tonight continuing to lie with how much of an impact 
there is on our forecast area. Models continue to the better 
potential being several hours off yet, and kept an mention of 
chances out through 00Z (some models say it could be closer to 
02-03Z). Through the overnight hours...there still some 
differences with just how much coverage there is, but general 
idea is that things end up staying on the more scattered side. 
Lift is aided by an increasing southwesterly LLJ, but the better
upper level forcing remains off to our north. Storm chances 
have other things working against there being greater coverage 
with time...loss of daytime heating. models showing warm mid-
level temps/capping remaining in place, and the further east 
things push, should push out of the area of better instability. 
Still not out of the question that a few storms early on could 
be on the strong to marginally severe side...and our WNW 
portions remain in the SPC Day 1 Marginal Risk area. Gusts near 
60 MPH and quarter size hail would be the primary hazards. 
Didn't get cute with PoPs through the overnight hours...pretty 
much anywhere could see at least an isolated shower/storm, so 
kept the 20 percent chances going CWA-wide. 

The main surface cold front will continue sinking south with
time overnight...by 12Z Tuesday, models are in pretty good 
agreement showing the front draped across the southeastern 
quarter or so of the forecast area. May end up with a gradient 
in lows tonight ranging from the upper 50s in the far NW to 
around 70 in the SE.

Tuesday and Wednesday...

Overall, no notable changes in the forecast for Tuesday and 
Wednesday...with continued precipitation chances and cooler 
temperatures still expected. Models remain in generally good 
agreement in the broader-scale. showing the upper level pattern 
remaining zonal across the Central Plains. Although on the 
weaker side, models showing the potential for enough lift 
lingering around to keep chances for at least spotty 
precipitation around for much of the day. Still some differences
and uncertainty with the overall coverage...and whether there 
is a bit stronger of a wave/more precip coverage as we get more 
into the evening/overnight hours into Wed AM. NBM have some 
widespread, higher PoPs between 06-18Z Wed (60-70 percent)...the
models supporting that timing show the better potential mainly 
across portions of south central NE. Still looking like the 
potential for severe weather is low, better instability should 
be becoming more focused to our south. With the increased cloud 
cover, precipitation chances, and continued northeasterly winds 
behind the cold front...high temperatures are forecast to range 
from the low 70s-low 80s on Tuesday to low-mid 70s for 
Wednesday.

Thursday and on...

For the end of this week on into the start of next week...again
not much as far as notable changes go in the forecast. Models 
continue to show the upper level pattern across the region in 
varying degrees of west-northwesterly flow. The main ridge tries
to build back north over the western CONUS...but additional 
larger-scale disturbances mainly moving across Canada prevent it
from amplifying too much. Precipitation chances Thursday 
through the weekend are spotty at best...and confidence in those
chances are certainly not high at this point. After the cooler
